candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care: practice within legal scope, recognize professional limitations and legal responsibilities, and provide care consistent with applicable laws/regulations and standards.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Nurse Practice Act, legal scope, and regulatory discipline
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that practicing outside legal nursing scope can lead to board-of-nursing discipline, with sanctions determined by the applicable Nurse Practice Act, jurisdiction, facts, severity, and disciplinary process rather than an automatic single penalty.

options.A: The board of nursing may impose discipline such as remediation, practice restrictions, suspension, or revocation, depending on applicable law and the facts of the case.
options.B: The consequence is limited to employer counseling because boards of nursing do not enforce Nurse Practice Acts.
options.C: Every scope violation automatically results in permanent license revocation regardless of severity, facts, or jurisdiction.
options.D: Every scope violation automatically produces a criminal conviction before any regulatory investigation or board proceeding occurs.

candidate.rationale: NCSBN explains that state boards of nursing enforce nursing laws and may take disciplinary action when a violation is established. Available board actions vary with state law and the facts and can include remediation or education, reprimand/fines, monitoring or probation, practice restrictions, suspension, and revocation or voluntary surrender. Therefore A is correct. B incorrectly denies board authority, while C and D falsely make one severe outcome automatic for every scope violation without investigation, due process, or jurisdiction-specific law.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A Nurse Practice Act/scope violation may lead to board discipline ranging from remediation or restrictions to suspension or revocation, with the actual action depending on state law and case facts.
candidate.source_document_title: Board Action; Discipline; Nurse Practice Act Toolkit
candidate.source_locator: Board Action > Disciplinary Actions: actions vary according to state law and may include monitoring/remediation/education, limitations or restrictions, suspension, revocation/surrender, fines and reprimands. NPA Toolkit: state Nurse Practice Acts establish BON authority and govern legal nursing practice.
